spans.s: Baka Dālbhya (‘descendant of Dalbha’) is the name of a person mentioned in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa as constraining indra for the Ājakeśins (i. 9, 2), and as a KuruPañcāla (iv. 7, 2).

Bakura is mentioned in one passage of the Rigveda, where it is said that the Aśvins made light for the Āryan by blowing their bakura against the Dasyus. According to the nirukta, the thunderbolt is meant; but much more probable is Roth's view, that the object blown was a musical instrument. See also bākura.

Bākura in one passage of the Rigveda (ix. 1, 8) is used as an epithet of dṛti, the combined words denoting a wind instrument of some kind. Cf. bakura.
